messages.author: bf2053d54b03b4e1
messages.subject: Lambert W function in RTMB
parts:
Hi all, 

First, apologies. Is there a RTMB equivalent mailing list that I should be using? Or somewhere else I should post RTMB questions? 

The question:
Does anyone know if RTMB has a native lambertW function that I could use?  something similar to the gsl::lambert_W0() in R. 

I want to use it to estimate the semelparous reference points described in: 

Scheuerell MD. 2016. An explicit solution for calculating optimum spawning stock size from Ricker’s stock recruitment model. PeerJ 4:e1623 https://doi.org/10.7717/peerj.1623

Thanks,

Catarina

messages.author: fd4f3538f907404b
messages.subject: Re: [TMB users] Lambert W function in RTMB
parts:
There's an example of a TMB-native Lambert W (that Kasper Kristensen
wrote when I needed it) here:

https://kaskr.github.io/adcomp/AtomicFunctions.html

I don't know how to integrate this into a TMB model (or if it's
straightforward) ...

messages.author: bf2053d54b03b4e1
messages.subject: Re: [TMB users] Lambert W function in RTMB
parts:
Hi everyone, 

Thank you for the quick response. Having a lambertW built-in in RTMB would be great for those of us doing Pacific salmon stock assessment. But the example you sent is working great. 

Also, I noticed that the lambertW in the example is not defined for negative values, which may be useful in some instances. For now we adapted the code from the lamW package, which is defined over a broader range.  Just another request to keep in mind in case you decide to add built-in functions. 

thanks again!

Catarina
